The answer to this broad query depends on the scope considered, as different sources address different regions and definitions. Within the United States, Native Hawaiians and other Pacific Islanders constitute the smallest minority group [d5]. In Vietnam, the Pu Peo is among the smallest recognized ethnic groups, with numbers as low as 687 in the 2009 census [d9]. Globally, the Toto people near the India-Bhutan border, with a population hovering around 2,000, are considered one of the world's smallest ethnic groups [d4]. Other sources identify the Abkhaz and Gagauz as among the world's smallest ethnic groups [d1], while in the context of uncontacted tribes, the 'Man of the Hole' — believed to be the sole surviving member of his tribe — represents the smallest known uncontacted ethnic group [d2]. Within U.S. ancestry self-identification, people identifying as 'Soviet Union' ancestry number only 832, making it the smallest self-reported ancestry group in the U.S. [d6].
